issue.title: SINP job-approval policy concerns
issue.summary: LinkedIn professionals criticize a historical pause in job approvals and its effects on employers and workers.
issue.concern: Professionals question pauses in immigration job approvals
issue.why: Professional commentary describes uncertainty around job-approval intake; affected applicants and dates are not verified in this supplementary topic.
issue.idea: Publish clear approved intake status and transition guidance first; staff may later use a cited policy-search assistant.
issue.limit: It cannot reopen intake, change nomination allocations or decide immigration eligibility.
issue.firstStep: Verify the referenced pause, dates and responsible provincial process, then identify any repeated unanswered administrative questions.
issue.measure: Enquiries receiving an accurate explanation of the current intake status and next applicable step.
issue.reason: Policy capacity and transitions appear primary; the evidence is supplementary and should not be treated as measured applicant demand.

route.title: SINP policy and application communication
route.ministry: Ministry of Immigration and Career Training
route.first: SINP / Immigration Services Branch for provincial nomination and job-approval questions.
route.escalation: Immigration and Career Training for provincial program administration. Federal nomination allocations and permanent-residence processing have separate federal responsibilities.
route.note: The linked posts describe a historical pause. Check current official program information for an actual case.

methodology: SK-C identifies a grouped concern. SK-E identifies an evidence record. These are internal research references, not official government complaint or case numbers.
A visible account counts once per concern. Repeat posts, votes, likes, unnamed relatives, organizations and deleted handles do not add people. Accounts are not verified individuals.
Named people in reporting are counted separately. They may overlap with online accounts and can describe the same incident. Do not add the two categories as unique people.
This brief includes every collected evidence record for this concern, regardless of dashboard filters. The reviewed sample is targeted, not a complete census or a measure of population prevalence.
Quotes document an expressed concern, not a verified finding of service failure. Historical resolutions, uncertainty and conflicting context are retained below.

AI ideas are proposals for investigation. They are not approved projects, verified root causes or promises of results. Authorized staff retain decisions about benefits, care, claims and other individual outcomes.

researchContext.scopeNote: The current 24-month window is 25 November 2024 to 25 November 2026. Moving the original window forward one day changes no included records. Undated LinkedIn leads are separate from the date-bounded counts.
limitations: This is a targeted public-source review, not an exhaustive search or representative survey. Counts describe the collected evidence.
All 70 observations from the original dashboard remain available. Six student-aid accounts and four date-unverified LinkedIn comments were added.
Social accounts are not verified people. Named complainants in reporting are a separate count; they may overlap with accounts.
A quoted post is evidence that someone expressed a concern, not proof of a service failure. Resolutions and conflicting context are retained.
Reddit and App Store evidence dominate the dated sample. Public-web searches cannot comprehensively cover X, LinkedIn, Quora, private groups or deleted content.
LinkedIn professional and advocacy comments are visible but lack verified calendar dates. They are tracked as leads and excluded from date-bounded account counts.
Some Reddit dates identify the parent discussion, not the exact comment. Do not infer daily trends from these dates.
AI opportunities are proposed discovery tasks. Some problems need clearer processes, reliable data or ordinary software fixes before AI is useful.
Benefits, clinical priority, claims, safeguarding and emergency decisions remain with authorized staff; the proposed AI work is assistance, not decision replacement.
Service responsibility can be shared: student aid spans the province, institutions and NSLSC; immigration allocations also involve the federal government.
A missing topic or platform means a gap in this review, not that nobody has complained about it.

researchContext.priorityMeaning: Suggested discovery order for a Solutions Architect, based on the reviewed complaints, clarity of the service problem and scope for a small pilot. This is judgment, not an objective score, prevalence ranking or incident-severity ranking.
